sensesIntro.en: Negligence starts as everyday carelessness, becomes a legal breach of duty, and is then graded by setting, by share of fault, and by seriousness.
sensesIntro.cn: negligence 从日常的粗心开始，转为法律上的违反注意义务，再按场景、过错份额与严重程度分级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opening instead of holding on.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该握紧的手却松开了。

branches.en: Everyday carelessness is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 日常的粗心是本义。

branches.en: A recognised duty turns carelessness into a legal wrong.
branches.cn: 被承认的注意义务把粗心变成法律上的不法。

branches.en: A professional standard raises the measure of care.
branches.cn: 职业标准抬高了注意的尺度。

branches.en: Shared fault and criminal fault show the same failure seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 分担过错与刑事过错是同一疏忽从两个方向看到的样子。

branches.en: Gross negligence marks the top of the scale before recklessness.
branches.cn: 重大过失标出轻率之前的最高一级。

intro.en: Negligence is built from the Latin neg- and legere, and English has grown a whole family around it.
intro.cn: negligence 由拉丁语 neg- 与 legere 构成，英语围绕它长出了整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin neglegere means to disregard, and its noun neglegentia means carelessness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neglegere 意为「不理」，其名词 neglegentia 意为「疏忽」。

items.example: The prefix neg- denies the act of picking up.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 neg- 否定了「拾起」这个动作。

items.example: Legere gives the image of taking something up.
items.exampleCN: legere 提供「把东西拾起来」的意象。

items.example: Neglegere joins the prefix to the verb.
items.exampleCN: neglegere 把前缀与动词合在一起。

items.example: Neglegentia is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: neglegentia 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Negligence keeps both the everyday and the legal sense.
items.exampleCN: negligence 同时保留日常与法律两种含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ence forms negligence from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 让拉丁词干构成 negligence。

items.meaningCN: 具有某种性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ent turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Neglect is the shorter verb from the same source.
items.exampleCN: neglect 是同源而来的较短动词。

items.example: Negligible shows how far the family can drift in meaning.
items.exampleCN: negligible 显示这个词族的意义可以漂移多远。

definition_zh: 可协商的；可转让兑现的；可通行的

senses.title: A price left open to bargaining
senses.titleCN: 价格留有余地，可以再谈
senses.definition: of a price or fee, not fixed, so that an offer below it may be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 指价格或费用没有定死，低于标价的出价也可能被接受
senses.example: The fee is negotiable if the work is finished early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果能提前完工，费用可以商量。
senses.why: the suffix -able turns the bargaining verb into a property: what can be bargained over is negotiable.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把「讨价还价」这个动作变成一种性质：能拿去谈的，就是 negotiable。

senses.title: Terms open to adjustment
senses.titleCN: 条款可以经过商谈改动
senses.definition: of clauses in a contract, capable of being changed by discussion
senses.definitionCN: 指合同中的条款能够通过商谈修改
senses.example: Every clause is negotiable except the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 除交货日期外，每一条款都可以商量。
senses.why: a clause is negotiable when it is still on the table, and closed when the parties stop talking about it.
senses.whyCN: 条款只要还在桌上，就是可谈的；双方不再谈它，就成了定局。

senses.title: Paper that can change hands
senses.definition: of a cheque, bill or note, legally transferable to another holder
senses.definitionCN: 指支票、汇票或本票在法律上可以转给另一个持有人
senses.example: A negotiable instrument can be passed on by endorsement.
senses.exampleCN: 可流通票据能通过背书转让。
senses.why: commerce reuses the bargaining idea: a bill whose ownership can be handed over is a bill that can be dealt with.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用「可谈」的思路：所有权能交出去的票据，就是能被处置的票据。

senses.title: A dispute that can be talked out
senses.titleCN: 争端可以通过谈判解决
senses.definition: of a conflict, capable of being settled by discussion rather than by force
senses.definitionCN: 指冲突能够通过商谈而非强制手段解决
senses.example: The dispute was negotiable, so no court action followed.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争议可以谈，因此没有走到诉讼。
senses.why: calling a dispute negotiable is a judgement about method: words may still work.
senses.whyCN: 说一场争端 negotiable，其实是在判断「办法」：话还管用。

senses.title: Ground that can be crossed
senses.definition: of a route, pass or slope, possible to travel over
senses.definitionCN: 指路线、隘口或坡面能够通行
senses.example: The pass is negotiable only from June to September.
senses.exampleCN: 这道隘口只有六月到九月可以通行。
senses.why: the physical branch of the verb survives here: what can be got through is literally negotiable.
senses.whyCN: 动词里那条「身体通过」的分支在此留存：能过得去的，字面上就是 negotiable。

senses.title: A person willing to bargain
senses.titleCN: 指人愿意谈、不把话堵死
senses.definition: of a person or a position, willing to discuss and give ground
senses.definitionCN: 指人或立场愿意商谈、肯作让步
senses.example: She remains negotiable on the price but not on the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 她在价格上仍可谈，在期限上则不让步。
senses.why: the adjective shifts from the matter to the holder: a person is negotiable when nothing is shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从「事情」移到「持事的人」：人 negotiable，是说他没有把门关死。

senses.title: A draft that can be cashed
senses.definition: of a draft, able to be paid out or accepted for value at a bank
senses.definitionCN: 指汇票能在银行兑现或被承付
senses.example: Travellers may find the draft negotiable at any branch.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客会发现这张汇票在任何一家分行都能兑付。
senses.why: banks say a draft is negotiable when they will buy it, which is the transfer sense seen from the counter.
senses.whyCN: 银行说一张汇票 negotiable，意思是它愿意买下它；这是从柜台那一侧看到的「转让」义。

senses.title: A clause open to periodic review
senses.titleCN: 条款按固定周期可再议
senses.definition: of a rent or a royalty, subject to renegotiation at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 指租金或提成按约定的周期可以重新商定
senses.example: The rent is negotiable every five years.
senses.exampleCN: 租金每五年可以重新议定一次。
senses.why: a review clause keeps an agreement deliberately unfinished, so the same adjective marks it.
senses.whyCN: 复审条款故意让协议「不封口」，于是同一个形容词也用来标记它。

intro.en: Negotiable is the Latin-derived bargaining verb plus -able, the ending that marks what can be done. It entered English through commercial law. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiable 是那个源自拉丁语的「谈判」动词加上 -able 构成，后者标记「可以被做」；它经商业法进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business' was built from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure', so trade was described as the absence of free time.
items.cn: negotium「生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成，于是「买卖」被描述为「没有空闲」。

items.en: The verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business', and its participle supplied the stem used by English.
items.cn: 动词 negotiari 意为「经商」，其分词提供英语所用的词干。

items.en: The ending -abilis marked what can be done or what serves a purpose; through French it became the English -able that builds hundreds of adjectives.
items.cn: 词尾 -abilis 标记「可被做」或「可供使用」；经法语变为英语的 -able，构成数以百计的形容词。

items.en: The adjective appears in English commercial writing in the eighteenth century, first of bills and notes that could be transferred.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪的商业文书中出现，最初用于可以转让的汇票与本票。

items.en: From paper the word spread to prices, contracts and finally to roads and slopes that can be got through.
items.cn: 从票据出发，这个词扩展到价格、合同，最后扩展到能过得去的道路与坡面。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest commercial citation is dated differently across dictionaries, and the deeper origin of otium is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对最早的商业书证年代说法不一；otium 的更早来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words whose endings make them look like relatives of this one; group two holds adjectives with a genuinely similar reach.
note.cn: 第一组收因词尾相似而看来像本词亲属的词；第二组收意义上确实相近的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare 'to sail', built on navis 'ship' and agere 'drive': a river that ships can pass, not a price that can be argued.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare「航行」，由 navis「船」与 agere「驾驶」构成：指可供船行的河，而非可议的价。

entries.definition: From negligere 'to disregard', built on legere 'to pick up'; it means too small to matter, with no bargaining sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 negligere「忽视」，由 legere「拾取」构成；意为小到可以忽略，与「谈判」无关。

entries.definition: The verb this adjective comes from: to bargain, or to get through a hard passage.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词所出的动词：讨价还价，或通过难走的一段。

entries.definition: The noun for the talking itself; the adjective describes a property of what that talking can change.
entries.definitionCN: 指商谈这件事本身的名词；形容词则描述「被商谈改变」的那种性质。

entries.definition: Able to be altered without breaking; broader than negotiable, which needs two parties to agree.
entries.definitionCN: 能改动而不折断；比 negotiable 宽，后者需要双方同意。

entries.definition: Able to be handed to another owner; it covers only the commercial branch of negotiable.
entries.definitionCN: 能交给另一个所有者的；只覆盖 negotiable 的商业那一支。

entries.definition: Open to dispute rather than open to a deal; a debatable point may never be settled by bargaining.
entries.definitionCN: 可以争论，而不是可以成交；可争之点未必能靠谈判定下来。

entries.definition: Liable to change without anyone deciding; negotiable implies the change would come from agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 会自行变动；而 negotiable 暗示变动来自双方同意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure' gives the business stem, and -able adds 'can be'.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」给出「生意」词干，-able 再加上「可以被」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, negotiability, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、negotiability、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split into two fields: a negotiable price, a negotiable instrument.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分成两个领域：可议的价格、可流通的票据。

normal.en: The usual negation is not a prefix but the phrase not open to negotiation.
normal.cn: 常见的否定并不是加前缀，而是「不容商量」这一说法。

normal.en: The opposite adjective non-negotiable is common in politics and in contracts.
normal.cn: 相反的形容词 non-negotiable 在政治与合同中都很常见。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag written in pencil rather than ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用铅笔而不是墨水写的价签。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose hinge is loose enough to open a little wider.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门的铰链松得还能再开一点。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge that sways but still carries a walker across.
abstract.cn: 想象一座会晃、却仍能把人送过对岸的索桥。

examples.en: The salary is negotiable, but the start date is not.
examples.cn: 薪资可以谈，入职日期不可以。

examples.en: Only the lower path is negotiable in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天只有下面那条小路能走。

examples.en: The note is negotiable at any bank in the city.
examples.cn: 这张本票在本市任何银行都可兑付。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「negotiate（谈判）+ able（能）」——能拿去谈的 → 可协商的

root: 拉丁 negotium（生意，字面「不得闲」）+ -abilis（可被……的）→ 英语 negotiable；商业法中最先指可转让票据，后扩展到价格、条款与可通行地形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: can this still be moved? A price, a clause, a bill, a dispute, a pass, a person, a draft and a rent clause can each be moved in a different way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：这东西还能不能动。价格、条款、票据、争端、隘口、人、汇票与租金条款，各自以不同方式「能动」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag written in pencil, with a small note in the margin saying it can still change.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张用铅笔写的价签，页边还有一行小字说这数字还能改。

branches.en: TALKABLE TERMS: a price and a clause stay unfinished while the parties keep talking.
branches.cn: 可谈的条款：只要双方还在谈，价格与条款就保持「未封口」。

branches.en: PAPER IN MOTION: a bill passes by endorsement, and a draft is bought at the counter.
branches.cn: 会动的纸：汇票靠背书传递，本票在柜台被买下。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND CONFLICTS: a quarrel can be talked out, and a person stays open to a deal.
branches.cn: 人与争端：争执可以谈开，人也始终留着成交的余地。

branches.en: GROUND: the old physical branch, where a pass opens for a few months each year.
branches.cn: 地形：最具体的一支，隘口每年只开放几个月。

branches.en: DELIBERATE GAP: a review clause keeps the agreement open on a schedule.
branches.cn: 刻意留的缝：复审条款按周期把协议重新打开。

intro.en: Negotiable is a Latin business noun turned into an adjective by a suffix that English borrowed and never stopped using.
intro.cn: negotiable 是一个拉丁「生意」名词，靠一个英语借来后一直沿用的后缀变成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun negotium and the verb negotiari supply the stem, while -abilis supplies the meaning of possibility.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 negotium 与动词 negotiari 提供词干，-abilis 提供「可能」之意。

definition_en: to discuss something in order to reach an agreement, or to get past a difficulty, a stretch of ground or a financial instrument
core_image: 两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，谁都没有停下，却都过去了

sceneCN: 这里 negotiate 指「为达成一致而反复商谈」（第 1 个义项：双方就条件来回商量）；句意为两家公司第三天再聚，就供货合同的条款进行谈判。可辨识物件：长桌、两份合同、钢笔、冷掉的茶；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Discuss in order to agree
senses.titleCN: 为达成一致而反复商谈
senses.definition: to talk with another party, trading proposals, until a shared position is reached
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方来回提出方案，直到达成共同的立场
senses.example: Union and management negotiated for eleven hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与资方谈了十一个小时。
senses.why: the Latin source means carrying on business, and bargaining is business conducted in words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「做买卖」，而讨价还价正是用言语做的买卖。

senses.title: Settle the terms of a deal
senses.definition: to settle a price, a contract or a release by bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价把价格、合同或释放条件定下来
senses.example: The captain negotiated the release of the crew.
senses.exampleCN: 船长谈成了船员的释放。
senses.why: the verb shifts from the talking to its product: what has been agreed now exists as terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从「谈」转向「谈出的结果」：已议定之事，如今作为条款存在。

senses.title: Get past a difficulty
senses.definition: to deal with an obstacle or a stage of a process successfully
senses.definitionCN: 成功地应付一处障碍或某个程序阶段
senses.example: The bill negotiated the committee stage intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案完整地通过了委员会阶段。
senses.why: a difficulty is treated like a stretch of road: you do not remove it, you get through it.
senses.whyCN: 难题被当成一段路来看：你不拆掉它，而是穿过去。

senses.title: Cross rough ground
senses.definition: to travel over or through a difficult physical passage
senses.definitionCN: 从一段难走的实际通道上通过
senses.example: Mules negotiate the narrow ledge without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 骡子毫不犹豫地走过那道窄石檐。
senses.why: this is the most physical branch: the bargaining skill of finding a way through becomes walking through.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的一支：谈判中「找出一条路」的本事，变成了真的走过去。

senses.title: Transfer or cash a draft
senses.definition: of a cheque or bill, to pass it to another party for value
senses.definitionCN: 指支票或汇票被交给另一方以取得对价
senses.example: The bank refused to negotiate the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 银行拒绝兑付这张汇票。
senses.why: a bill of exchange is a promise passed from hand to hand, and the verb names that passing.
senses.whyCN: 汇票是一张在人与人之间传递的承诺，这个动词命名的正是这次传递。

senses.title: Carry on trade
senses.definition: to buy and sell, to conduct business, in the older commercial sense
senses.definitionCN: 买卖货物、经营生意，属较早的商业用法
senses.example: Merchants negotiated in spices and tin.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们在香料与锡之间做买卖。
senses.why: the original Latin verb meant exactly this; the diplomatic sense is the later narrowing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原动词正是这个意思；后来外交上的用法才是收窄出来的。

senses.title: Obtain by bargaining
senses.definition: to secure a benefit for oneself or others through bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价为自己或他人争得某种好处
senses.example: She negotiated a shorter working week for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她为整个团队争得了更短的工作周。
senses.why: negotiating is not only meeting the other side halfway; it is also extracting a concession from them.
senses.whyCN: 谈判不只是各让一步，也是从对方那里争得一项让步。

senses.title: Manage a passage successfully
senses.definition: to handle a vehicle or a situation through a hazardous passage
senses.definitionCN: 把车辆或局面稳稳地带过一段危险路程
senses.example: The pilot negotiated the storm with steady hands.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员稳稳地把飞机带过了暴风雨。
senses.why: when the obstacle is weather or traffic, the word describes control rather than talking.
senses.whyCN: 当障碍是天气或车流时，这个词描述的是「掌控」，而不是「商谈」。

intro.en: Negotiate comes from Latin negotiari 'to carry on business', from negotium 'business', literally 'not-leisure'. The agreement sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiate 来自拉丁 negotiari「做买卖」，其名词 negotium「事务、生意」字面是「不得闲」。表示「达成协议」的义项是后来收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business, affair' was formed from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure': business is the state in which one has no leisure.
items.cn: negotium「事务、生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成：生意就是「不得闲」的状态。

items.en: The deponent verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business, to trade', and negotiator named the merchant who did so.
items.cn: 异态动词 negotiari 意为「经营、买卖」，negotiatio 与 negotiator 分别指经商这件事与经商的商人。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century first in the commercial sense of trading and dealing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初正是「做买卖、经营」的商业义。

items.en: The sense of conferring with someone, talking a matter over, appears next, still without any promise of agreement.
items.cn: 接着出现「与人商议、把事情谈一谈」的义项，当时仍不含达成协议的承诺。

items.en: Diplomacy fixed the modern sense: to confer with a view to reaching terms, and later to settle those terms.
items.cn: 外交用法固定了现代义：为议定条件而商谈，后来又指把这些条件谈成。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the boundary between the conferring sense and the settling sense is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the earlier history of otium beyond Latin is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对「商议」与「谈成」两义的分界年代说法不一；otium 在拉丁语之前的来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the shape of the ending but come from unrelated Latin verbs; group two holds verbs that also settle matters between people.
note.cn: 第一组收词尾形状相同、却出自互不相干的拉丁动词的词；第二组收同样在人与人之间把事定下来的动词。

entries.definition: From Latin negare 'to deny', built on neg- 'not'; it means to deny or make ineffective, with no link to business.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 negare「否认」，由 neg-「不」构成；意为否定或使失效，与「生意」无关。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare, built on navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive'; it means to steer a course, not to bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare，由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成；意为掌舵行船，而非讨价还价。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same verb: open to being discussed, or able to be transferred.
entries.definitionCN: 同出于这个动词的形容词：可以商量的，或可以转让的。

entries.definition: The prefixed form: to open the terms of an agreement again and bargain them afresh.
entries.definitionCN: 加前缀的形式：重新打开已达成的条件再谈一遍。

entries.definition: To argue over price or terms in a market; it is the everyday, usually smaller-scale word.
entries.definitionCN: 在市场上为价格或条件争来讲去；是日常、通常规模较小的说法。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them agree; the mediator may not be a party to the deal.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间帮助他们达成一致；调停者本身可能并非交易的一方。

entries.definition: To arrange a deal between others, often for a fee; the broker acts on behalf of the parties.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人安排交易，常收取费用；经纪人代表当事人行事。

entries.definition: To bring a dispute to an end and fix the terms; it names the closing moment rather than the talking.
entries.definitionCN: 把争端结束并定下条件；命名的是收尾那一刻，而不是商谈过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure': business is literally the opposite of free time.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」：生意字面上就是「没有闲功夫」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with contracts and prices: negotiate a contract, negotiate a price.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与合同、价格配在一起：协商合同、商议价格。

normal.en: The same verb crosses obstacles: negotiate a bend, negotiate the narrow ledge.
normal.cn: 同一个动词也用于越过障碍：通过弯道、走过窄石檐。

normal.en: Banks negotiate drafts, so the word appears in finance as well as diplomacy.
normal.cn: 银行会兑付汇票，因此这个词既在外交也在金融里出现。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one table through a narrow door, each tilting his own end.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一张桌子过窄门，各抬自己那一头并各自倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from both banks until it is taut but not broken.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳从两岸同时收紧，绷直却没有断。

abstract.en: Picture a path that exists only where two sets of footprints overlap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只存在于两串脚印重合处的路。

examples.en: The two governments negotiated for months before signing anything.
examples.cn: 两国政府在签字之前谈了好几个月。

examples.en: He negotiated a lower rent by offering to repair the roof himself.
examples.cn: 他提出自己修屋顶，以此谈低了房租。

examples.en: The old road negotiates the cliff in a series of tight turns.
examples.cn: 那条老路用一连串急弯绕过悬崖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ne（不）+ goti（闲）+ ate」——不得闲，就得去谈生意 → 谈判

root: 拉丁 negotiari「经商」出自 negotium「事务、生意」= neg-（不）+ otium（闲暇）；「谈成协议」义为后世收窄而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from business as the opposite of leisure: people talk terms, terms harden into a deal, and the same knack of getting through is then applied to obstacles, ground, storm and paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「生意即不得闲」出发：人们先谈条件，条件凝成交易，随后同一套「过得去」的本事被用于障碍、地形、风暴与票据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two boats in a narrow channel each give half a rudder and both pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，双方都过去了。

branches.en: TALKING INTO TERMS: proposals move between the parties until a deal exists.
branches.cn: 谈出条款：方案在双方之间来回，直到交易成形。

branches.en: CONTROLLED PASSAGE: a bill or an aircraft is brought through a hard stretch without damage.
branches.cn: 稳妥通过：法案或飞机被稳稳带过一段难走的路。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND COMMERCIAL ROOT: crossing ground and trading goods are the two oldest branches.
branches.cn: 路与货：穿越地形与买卖货物，是最老的两支。

branches.en: PAPER PASSED ON: a draft changes hands, and the verb names the passing.
branches.cn: 票据易手：汇票从一只手到另一只手，动词命名的正是这次传递。

branches.en: GAIN EXTRACTED: bargaining is also the art of pulling a concession toward oneself.
branches.cn: 争得好处：谈判也是把让步拉向自己这一边的本事。

intro.en: Negotiate is a Latin verb made of a negative particle and a noun for leisure, which is why the family can be read as a small sentence about work.
intro.cn: negotiate 是一个由否定小品词与「闲暇」之名词构成的拉丁动词，因此这个词族可以读成一句关于「工作」的小句子。

latinIntro.en: Latin negotium yields negotiari, negotiator and negotiatio, and those in turn give the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 negotium 衍生 negotiari、negotiator 与 negotiatio，这些又衍生出英语的整个词族。

items.example: The particle turns leisure into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个小品词把「闲暇」变成「不得闲」。

items.example: The noun supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的后一半。

items.example: The compound began as a description of work.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词最初是对「工作」的描述。

items.example: The verb entered English through this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的动词正是经这个形式传入。
他们就合同进行了谈判。

items.meaning: able to be discussed or transferred

items.example: The lease was renegotiated last spring.
items.exampleCN: 租约去年春天重新谈过。

latinEntries.structure: negotiari, negotiatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)

definition_zh: 谈判；协商；议价；通过（弯道、障碍）；（票据）兑现
definition_en: the process of discussing something in order to reach an agreement, or the successful passing of a difficult route or a financial instrument
core_image: 两个人隔桌而坐，桌上摊着一张纸，各自把笔移到中间那条线的两侧。
scene: 两家公司在会议室里逐条修改合同，先把价格放一边。They began a long negotiation over delivery dates.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiation 是“为达成协议而进行的谈判”（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们开始就交货日期进行长时间的谈判；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 谈判；协商；议价；（弯道、障碍的）通过；（票据的）兑现、转让

derivatives.zh: 谈判；协商；通过（险处）；兑现（票据）
谈判者；协商代表
可谈判的；可兑现的
重新谈判；重新协商

senses.title: Talk aimed at agreement
senses.definition: the process of discussion between parties who want an agreement but do not yet share the same terms
senses.definitionCN: 希望达成协议但条件尚未一致的各方向进行讨论的过程
senses.example: The negotiation lasted three days before both sides signed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判持续了三天，双方才签字。
senses.why: The word names the whole process, not one offer: parties move positions until a text can be accepted by both.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整个过程，而不是某一次报价：各方不断移动立场，直到出现双方都能接受的文本。

senses.title: Bargaining over price and terms
senses.titleCN: 议价磋商：一项一项地换条件
senses.definition: bargaining in which price, quantity, delivery, or other terms are traded against each other
senses.definitionCN: 就价格、数量、交货或其他条款相互交换让步的讨价还价
senses.example: The price was settled in a separate negotiation over volume discounts.
senses.exampleCN: 价格在另一场关于批量折扣的议价中确定。
senses.why: Commerce turns agreement into a trade of terms: one side gives on price, the other gives on time, and the sum must still balance.
senses.whyCN: 商业把协议变成条款交换：一方在价格上让步，另一方在时间上让步，总和仍须平衡。

senses.title: Diplomatic bargaining
senses.titleCN: 外交谈判：国家之间的文字较量
senses.definition: formal talks between states or political groups, often over conflict, borders, or treaties
senses.definitionCN: 国家或政治集团之间就冲突、边界或条约进行的正式会谈
senses.example: The peace negotiation produced a ceasefire but no final border.
senses.exampleCN: 和平谈判带来了停火，却没有确定最终边界。
senses.why: When the parties are states, the same process carries public authority: what is agreed becomes a document that binds populations, not just signers.
senses.whyCN: 当各方是国家时，同一过程带有公共权威：谈成的内容会成为约束民众而不仅是签字者的文件。

senses.title: Dealing over work and pay
senses.titleCN: 合同薪酬谈判：把自己的条件摆上桌
senses.definition: talks between an employer and an employee or union about wages, hours, and working conditions
senses.definitionCN: 雇主与雇员或工会就工资、工时与劳动条件进行的会谈
senses.example: Her salary negotiation gained a raise and an extra week of leave.
senses.exampleCN: 她的薪酬谈判争取到了加薪和额外一周假期。
senses.why: Here the abstract process becomes personal: the terms being traded are the conditions of one's daily life, so preparation and timing matter.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象过程变得切身：被交换的条款是一个人日常生活的条件，因此准备与时机都很重要。

senses.title: Getting a vehicle round a bend
senses.titleCN: 过弯：把车身稳稳带过弯道
senses.definition: the act of steering or driving a vehicle safely through a curve or narrow passage
senses.definitionCN: 操纵车辆安全通过弯道或狭窄路段的行为
senses.example: The bus slowed for the sharp negotiation of the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 大巴减速以通过山路的急弯。
senses.why: From 'dealing with a difficulty' comes the physical sense: the driver negotiates the curve as a rider negotiates a rough path.
senses.whyCN: 从“应对困难”引申出物理义：司机把车稳稳带过弯道，就像骑手带马穿过一段崎岖小路。

senses.title: Passing an obstacle
senses.titleCN: 越过险处：从障碍中穿过去
senses.definition: the successful passing of a physical obstruction, such as a fence, a reef, or rough ground
senses.definitionCN: 成功穿过栅栏、暗礁或崎岖地面等物理障碍
senses.example: The boat's negotiation of the reef took all the crew's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 船只穿越暗礁的过程让全体船员全神贯注。
senses.why: The sense keeps the core idea of dealing with something difficult, but the difficulty is now ground or water rather than another person.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留“应对难事”的核心意思，但难事从“另一个人”变成了地面或水面。

senses.title: Cashing or transferring an instrument
senses.titleCN: 票据兑现：让一张纸变成钱
senses.definition: the passing of a cheque, bill, or other financial instrument through the banking system so that it is paid or transferred
senses.definitionCN: 让支票、汇票等金融票据经银行系统完成付款或转让
senses.example: The negotiation of the cheque failed because the signature did not match.
senses.exampleCN: 这张支票因签名不符而未能兑现。
senses.why: A financial instrument must also be 'carried through' a system; the old commercial sense of negotiation survives in banking as the successful passage of paper.
senses.whyCN: 金融票据也必须“穿过”一套系统；negotiation 古老的商业义项在银行领域以“票据顺利通过”的形式留存下来。

senses.title: Agreeing on what words mean
senses.titleCN: 意义协商：边说边确认对方懂了
senses.definition: the interactive process by which speakers adjust wording until both understand a meaning in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 说话者调整措辞，直到双方以相同方式理解某一含义的互动过程
senses.example: In the language class, the negotiation of meaning happened through gestures and repetition.
senses.exampleCN: 在语言课上，意义协商通过手势和重复完成。
senses.why: Even without a contract, two minds must reach a shared version of what a word refers to; that temporary agreement is a negotiation too.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有合同，两个头脑也必须就一个词指什么达成共同版本；这种临时一致同样是一场谈判。

intro.en: Negotiation comes from Latin negotiatio, business or trade, from negotiari, to do business, and negotium, a matter of business. Its literal makeup is 'not leisure'.
intro.cn: negotiation 来自拉丁语 negotiatio“生意、交易”，出自动词 negotiari“做买卖”与名词 negotium“事务、业务”。其字面构成是“不闲暇”。

items.en: Otium meant leisure, ease, or time free from public affairs. It is the peaceful half of the word's ancestry.
items.cn: otium 意为闲暇、安逸，或免于公共事务的时间；它是这个词祖先中安静的那一半。

items.en: Negotium joined nec- 'not' to otium: not-leisure, hence business, employment, and a matter requiring effort.
items.cn: negotium 把 nec-“不”与 otium 结合：不闲暇，因而指业务、职务，以及需要费力的事务。

items.en: The verb meant to carry on business, to trade, and also to transact or manage a matter.
items.cn: 该动词意为做买卖、从事交易，也指经办或处理一桩事务。

items.en: The noun named business, traffic in goods, and the conduct of a transaction. It did not yet mean formal talks.
items.cn: 该名词指生意、货物交易以及交易的处理，当时还没有“正式会谈”的意思。

items.en: French narrowed the word toward the talks that precede a transaction, and English borrowed that sense in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语把词义收窄到交易之前的商谈，英语在 16 世纪借入了这一含义。

items.en: Diplomacy, labour relations, and banking each kept a branch: talks, bargaining, and the passing of an instrument through a system.
items.cn: 外交、劳资关系与银行各自保留了一条分支：会谈、议价，以及票据在系统中的通过。

note.en: The first group is the negotiate family; the second compares ways of settling a difference, from friendly talk to third-party decision.
note.cn: 第一组是 negotiate 词族；第二组比较解决分歧的方式，从友好商谈到第三方裁决。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to agree, or to get past a difficulty. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成一致而商谈，或越过困难；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: a person who takes part in talks on behalf of a side. It names the actor, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 代表一方参加谈判的人；命名的是行动者，不是过程。

entries.definition: open to being changed by agreement, or able to be transferred as payment. It describes a quality of terms.
entries.definitionCN: 可经协商改变的，或可作为支付转让的；描述条款的性质。

entries.definition: hard trading of offers, especially over price. It sounds more competitive than negotiation.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕报价的强硬交换，尤指价格；比 negotiation 更有竞争味。

entries.definition: help from a neutral third party to reach agreement. The parties still decide, but someone else runs the talk.
entries.definitionCN: 由中立第三方协助达成协议；仍由当事方决定，但谈话由他人主持。

entries.definition: settlement by an outside judge whose decision binds the parties. It replaces negotiation with a ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 由外部裁决者作出有约束力的决定；以裁决取代谈判。

entries.definition: asking for opinions before deciding. It gathers views but does not require agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前征求意见；收集看法，但不要求达成一致。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: nec- 'not' plus otium 'leisure'. Business is literally not-leisure, and negotiation is the talk that business requires.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：nec-“不”加 otium“闲暇”。业务字面上就是“不闲暇”，而 negotiation 是业务所需的商谈。

normal.en: Not-leisure: the moment people stop relaxing and start trading terms.
normal.cn: 不闲暇：人们停止放松、开始交换条件的那一刻。

normal.en: A negotiation is a table with two pens and one text between them.
normal.cn: 谈判就是一张桌子、两支笔，以及中间那一份文本。

normal.en: In banking, negotiation is paper passing through a system; in driving, it is a car passing through a curve.
normal.cn: 在银行，negotiation 是票据穿过系统；在驾驶，是车穿过弯道。

normal.en: Salary negotiation trades hours of your life for a number on a contract.
normal.cn: 薪酬谈判用你生命中的小时数换合同上的一个数字。

normal.en: Language learners negotiate meaning with gestures before they find the word.
normal.cn: 语言学习者先用手势协商意义，然后才找到那个词。

abstract.en: Negotiation begins only where two sides are both dependent and unwilling to lose the other.
abstract.cn: 谈判只始于双方既相互依赖、又不愿失去对方的地方。

abstract.en: The word's ancestry says business is the absence of leisure; the modern noun says agreement is the absence of easy silence.
abstract.cn: 这个词的祖先说业务是闲暇的缺席；现代名词则说协议是轻松沉默的缺席。

abstract.en: To negotiate a bend is to accept that the path will not be straight; every agreement has a curve built into it.
abstract.cn: 把车带过一个弯道，就是接受道路不会笔直；每份协议里都内置了一道弯。

examples.en: The union entered negotiations with a single demand: a fixed schedule two weeks in advance.
examples.cn: 工会带着一项诉求进入谈判：提前两周给出固定排班。

examples.en: Years of practice let the old driver negotiate the narrow bridge without slowing much.
examples.cn: 多年练习让老司机几乎不减速就通过了那座窄桥。

examples.en: The cheque failed negotiation because the account had been closed.
examples.cn: 这张支票未能兑现，因为账户已经销户。

dict_mnemonic.text: nego（不）+ tiation（歇）——不歇着，坐下来谈条件，就是谈判。

root: 源自拉丁语 negotiatio（生意、交易），出自 negotium（事务、业务），字面为 nec-“不”+ otium“闲暇”，即“不闲暇之事”；后经法语收窄为“交易前的商谈”，再扩展出外交、劳资、过弯与票据兑现等义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of negotiation. The core is always a difficult passage made manageable: two sides pass from disagreement to agreement, a driver passes a curve, a cheque passes through a bank, or two speakers pass into shared meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: negotiation 的八个义项，核心始终是“让一段难走的路变得可走”：双方从分歧走到一致，司机通过弯道，支票穿过银行系统，两个说话者进入共同理解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at a table, one sheet of paper, and each pen moving toward the middle line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔桌，一张纸，两支笔各自向中间那条线移动。

chain: FRENCH NEGOCIATION TALKS BEFORE A DEAL
ENGLISH NEGOTIATION THE PROCESS OF REACHING TERMS

branches.en: MAKING A DEAL: the general process and the item-by-item trade of price and terms.
branches.cn: 达成交易：一般谈判过程，与逐项交换价格和条款的议价。

branches.en: TALKS WITH WEIGHT: state-to-state diplomacy and employer-to-employee bargaining.
branches.cn: 有分量的会谈：国家对国家的外交，与雇主对雇员的劳资谈判。

branches.en: PHYSICAL PASSAGE: steering through a bend and passing a reef or rough ground.
branches.cn: 物理通过：驾车过弯，以及穿过暗礁或崎岖地面。

branches.en: FINANCIAL PASSAGE: a cheque or bill carried through the banking system.
branches.cn: 金融通过：支票或汇票经银行系统完成流转。

branches.en: SHARED MEANING: speakers adjusting words until both mean the same thing.
branches.cn: 共享意义：说话者调整措辞，直到双方所指相同。

intro.en: Negotiation is negotiate plus -ion, the action-noun suffix. The family adds -or for the person, -able for what can be traded or changed, and re- for doing it again.
intro.cn: negotiation 是 negotiate 加 -ion（动作名词后缀）。词族用 -or 表示人，-able 表示可交易或可更改，re- 表示重新进行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is otium, leisure, negated by nec-. Negotium and negotiari are the business words built on that negation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 otium“闲暇”，由 nec- 否定。negotium 与 negotiari 就是建立在这一否定之上的业务用语。

items.meaning: leisure, ease, freedom from public business
items.meaningCN: 闲暇；安逸；免于公共事务
items.example: Otium in Roman life meant time for letters and thought.
items.exampleCN: 在罗马生活中，otium 指用于写信与思考的时间。

items.meaning: to discuss for agreement, or to get past a difficulty
items.meaningCN: 为达成协议而商谈，或越过困难
items.example: They negotiated the price down by ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 他们把价格谈低了百分之十。

items.meaning: the process of bargaining or passing a difficulty
items.meaningCN: 谈判过程，或通过困难的过程
items.example: The negotiation produced a draft both sides could sign.
items.exampleCN: 谈判产生了一份双方都能签署的草案。

items.example: The chief negotiator asked for a short break.
items.exampleCN: 首席谈判代表要求短暂休息。

items.meaning: open to agreement, or legally transferable
items.meaningCN: 可协商的，或可依法转让的
items.example: The delivery date is still negotiable.
The landlord agreed to renegotiate the lease.
items.exampleCN: 房东同意重新协商租约。

items.meaning: a merchant or dealer, now rare
items.example: The old records list him as a negotiant in silk.
items.exampleCN: 旧档案把他记为丝绸商人。

items.meaning: settled by talks rather than by rule
items.meaningCN: 经谈判议定的，而非按规定定的
items.example: The workers returned under a negotiated settlement.
items.exampleCN: 工人们在谈判达成的解决方案下复工。

definition_zh: 邻居；邻人；邻近的人或物；毗邻
definition_en: a person who lives next door or close by; a person or thing standing beside another; and, as a verb, to be next to a place
core_image: 两家院墙之间只隔一道矮篱，篱上晾着同一根绳子上的衣物
scene: 楼道里的纸箱还没拆完，对门的人先端来一壶热水。The neighbour across the hall brought a kettle of hot water before the boxes were even opened.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbour 是「邻居」（第 1 个义项：住在近旁的人）；句意为纸箱还没打开，对门那位就端来一壶热水。图中可辨识物件：楼道、纸箱、水壶。

pos.zh: 邻居；邻近的人或物
邻近；毗邻

derivatives.zh: 由 neighbour 加 -ing 构成，义为「邻近的；相邻的」
由 neighbour 加 -ly 构成，义为「邻里般的；友善的」
由 neighbourly 加 -ness 构成，义为「邻里情谊；友善」
neighbourhood 的美式拼写，义为「街区；邻里」

senses.title: A person who lives close by
senses.definition: someone who lives next door or very near to one's home
senses.definitionCN: 住在隔壁或离家很近的人
senses.example: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。
senses.why: The Old English compound joins neah, near, with gebur, a dweller, so the word names the person who dwells near you rather than a friend or a relative.
senses.whyCN: 古英语复合词把 neah（近）与 gebur（居住者）拼在一起，字面上指的就是「住得近的人」，与朋友或亲戚无关。

senses.title: A person or thing placed beside another
senses.definition: the person sitting or standing beside you, or a thing lying next to another of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 坐在或站在你旁边的人，或与其他同类相邻的事物
senses.example: She leaned towards her neighbour at the table to hear the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她凑向同桌的邻座，想听清祝酒词。
senses.why: Because the word marks only position, it can be used for a stranger in the next seat, and the same logic lets it describe a country lying beside another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只标记位置，所以能用来指旁边座位上的陌生人，同样的逻辑也让它可以形容一个挨着另一个的国家。

senses.title: To stand next to a place
senses.definition: to be situated immediately beside or near a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 位于某处紧邻的位置
senses.example: The small farm neighbours a protected stretch of river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。
senses.why: Having named the dweller nearby, English turns the word into a verb for the dwelling itself standing beside another, which is a short step from a person to a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然已经指「住在近旁的人」，英语就把这个词改成动词，指房屋本身紧挨着另一处；从人到地点只差一小步。

intro.en: Neighbour is an Old English compound of two plain words, one meaning near and one meaning dweller. The British spelling keeps ou, and American English writes neighbor.
intro.cn: neighbour 是古英语里两个很朴素的词拼成的，一个表示「近」，一个表示「居住者」。英式拼写保留 ou，美式写作 neighbor。

items.en: The first element goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for near, the same source as near and the archaic nigh.
items.cn: 第一个成分可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「近」的重构词根，与 near、古旧的 nigh 同源。

items.en: Neah meant near or close, and it survives as the first half of the compound neahgebur.
items.cn: neah 意为近、靠近，作为复合词 neahgebur 的前半保留下来。

items.en: Gebur meant a dweller or a fellow worker of the land, so neahgebur was the person living close by.
items.cn: gebur 指居住者或一同种地的人，所以 neahgebur 就是住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the word as neighebor, and the vowel and spelling shifted several times before settling.
items.cn: 中古英语把它改写成 neighebor，元音和拼写来回变过几次才固定下来。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbour with ou, while American English simplifies it to neighbor; the meaning and the history are the same.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留带 ou 的 neighbour，美式简化为 neighbor；两者的含义与来历完全相同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the near element or merely the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who live in a place.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「近」这一成分的词，以及只是读音相近的词；近义组收表示住在某处的人。

entries.definition: Close in space or time, the idea that also sits inside the first half of neighbour.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上接近的；neighbour 的前半也藏着这个「近」的想法。

entries.definition: An older word for near, now mostly literary or dialectal.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「近」的较古老词，现多用于文学或方言。

entries.definition: The long loud cry of a horse; it only looks and sounds like neighbour, and its root is imitative.
entries.definitionCN: 马的长嘶声；只是与 neighbour 形音相近，词源是拟声，二者无关。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 住在某个地方的人；居民。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular house or area, often used in compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 住在某处房屋或地区的人，常用于复合词。

entries.definition: A person who lives in the area being talked about.
entries.definitionCN: 住在所谈地区的人；本地人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of near and dweller, and the British spelling keeps an ou that American English drops.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「近」与「居住者」复合而成，英式拼写保留一个美式会去掉的 ou。

normal.en: Neah means near and gebur means dweller, so a neighbour is simply the dweller nearest to you.
normal.cn: neah 意为近，gebur 意为居住者，所以邻居就是离你最近的居住者。

normal.en: The -bour part is the old word for a dweller, not the English word for a harbour, so do not read it as a port.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 -bour 是古语「居住者」，不是英语里表示港口的词，别把它读成码头。

normal.en: The verb use follows the noun, since a farm can neighbour a river: the word only marks what stands close.
normal.cn: 动词用法跟着名词走，农场可以 neighbour 一条河，因为这个词只标记「紧挨着」的位置。

normal.en: American English writes neighbor, and the shorter form follows the same pattern as harbor and color.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighbor，缩短的拼写与 harbor、color 遵循同一规律。

normal.en: Next-door neighbour is the fixed phrase for the person in the house beside yours.
normal.cn: next-door neighbour 是固定说法，指紧挨着你家的那户人。

abstract.en: A word built from near and dweller turns geography into a relationship: closeness itself becomes a kind of company.
abstract.cn: 一个由「近」和「居住者」拼成的词，把地理变成关系：距离近本身就成了一种陪伴。

abstract.en: The British ou and the American missing u are the same word wearing two passports.
abstract.cn: 英式多写一个 u、美式省掉它，是同一个词拿着两本护照。

abstract.en: Calling a country a neighbour borrows the warmth of a doorstep for something as cold as a border.
abstract.cn: 把一个国家叫作 neighbour，是把门槛边的暖意借给了边界这样冰冷的东西。

examples.en: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
examples.cn: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。

examples.en: She turned to her neighbour at the table and smiled.
examples.cn: 她转向同桌的邻座，笑了一下。

examples.en: The farm neighbours a stretch of protected river.
examples.cn: 这座农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内个伯」——巷子里那位伯伯就住在隔壁，张嘴一喊就是他；记住 neighbour 是邻居。

root: 古英语 neah（近）加 gebur（居住者）复合为 neahgebur，中古英语作 neighebor，现代英式拼写 neighbour，美式拼写 neighbor。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who dwells near; from that, the meaning widens to anyone or anything beside you and then becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「住得不远的人」；由此词义扩到身边任何人或物，最后又变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low hedge between two yards, with washing hung across it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两家院子之间一道矮篱，篱上晾着同一根绳子上的衣物。

branches.en: a kettle handed over a shared doorstep
branches.cn: 从共用的门槛递过来的一壶水

branches.en: two families hanging washing on one line
branches.cn: 两家人把衣服晾在同一根绳上

branches.en: a stranger in the next seat on a long flight
branches.cn: 长途航班上邻座的陌生人

branches.en: a farm fence running beside a river
branches.cn: 沿着河边伸长的农场篱笆

branches.en: a border stone that two gardens share
branches.cn: 两个花园共用的一块界石

intro.en: The word is a compound of an old adjective for near and a noun for dweller, and English later added endings that make it an adjective and a noun of quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「近」的古形容词与表示「居住者」的名词复合而成，英语后来又加上词尾，使它成为形容词和表示情谊的名词。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic in origin and has no reliable Latin cognate; its parts and its family are Old English and English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它的构件和词族都属于古英语和英语。

items.meaning: dweller, fellow worker of the land
a person living near; to adjoin

definition_zh: 神经；勇气；胆量；放肆；紧张不安；鼓起勇气
definition_en: a fibre that carries signals in the body; courage to do something difficult; bold rudeness; a state of nervous tension; to give oneself courage
core_image: 一根细长的白线从脊柱伸向指尖，轻轻一碰就传来一阵电流
scene: 冬天的早晨，厨房的水壶在响，母亲搓着手站在门口，声音有些发抖。I did not have the nerve to tell her the truth.
sceneCN: 这里是「胆量、勇气」（第 2 个义项：做难事所需的胆量）；句意为我没有勇气把实情告诉她。图中可辨识物件：冒着热气的水壶、门口的双手。

pos.zh: 神经；勇气；胆量；放肆；紧张不安
使鼓起勇气；给……打气

derivatives.zh: 由 nerve 加 -ous 构成，义为「紧张的；神经的」
由 nervous 加 -ly 构成，义为「紧张地；不安地」
由 nervous 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧张；神经质」
由拉丁前缀 e-（去掉）加 nervus 构成，义为「使失去活力」

senses.title: A fibre carrying signals between the brain and the body
senses.definition: a long fibre in the body that carries messages between the brain, the senses and the muscles
senses.definitionCN: 体内传递信息的长纤维，连接大脑、感官与肌肉
senses.example: The dentist damaged a nerve in my jaw.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医伤到了我下颌的一根神经。
senses.why: Latin nervus first named a sinew or tendon, the visible white cord in a body; anatomists then gave that same cord the job of carrying feeling, and the word kept the picture of a thread running through flesh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nervus 最初指筋或肌腱，也就是身体里看得见的白色细索；解剖学家随后让这同一根索承担传递感觉的职责，这个词便保留了「细线穿过血肉」的画面。

senses.title: Courage to face something difficult
senses.definition: the steady confidence needed to do something frightening or demanding
senses.definitionCN: 面对可怕或艰难之事时所需的稳定信心
senses.example: The climber finally lost his nerve near the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 那名登山者在接近山顶时终于失去了勇气。
senses.why: Sinews are what keep a body taut and steady, so to have nerve came to mean to hold that taut strength when fear pulls at it; courage is the sinew of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 筋让身体绷紧、稳住，因此 to have nerve 就指在恐惧拉扯时仍保持那种绷紧的力量；勇气成了心智的筋。

senses.title: Bold impudence that ignores what others expect
senses.definition: rude boldness shown by doing something others consider too cheeky
senses.definitionCN: 做出别人认为太冒失的事而显出的无礼大胆
senses.example: He had the nerve to ask for a second raise.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟厚着脸皮要求再加一次薪。
senses.why: The same strength that deserves praise can also be judged as bare-faced boldness when it ignores other people's feelings, so a word for taut power slides into a word for cheek.
senses.whyCN: 同一种值得称赞的力量，一旦无视别人的感受，也会被判为赤裸裸的放肆；于是表示「绷紧之力」的词滑成了表示「厚脸皮」的词。

senses.title: A state of nervous tension, usually in the plural
senses.definition: a feeling of being anxious and unable to relax, commonly used as the plural nerves
senses.definitionCN: 焦虑、无法放松的感觉，常用复数形式
senses.example: She had a bad case of nerves before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试之前她紧张得厉害。
senses.why: Nerves were understood as the body's sensitive cords, so when those cords were overexcited the name moved from the fibres to the feeling they produced; a case of nerves is the body reporting on itself.
senses.whyCN: nerves 被理解为身体里敏感的细索，当这些索过度兴奋时，名称就从纤维转到它们产生的感觉；a case of nerves 就是身体在报告自己的状态。

senses.title: To give oneself or another person courage
senses.definition: to make oneself or someone else brave enough to do something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或别人有足够勇气去做难事
senses.example: He nerved himself to knock on the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他鼓起勇气去敲门。
senses.why: Turning the noun into a verb makes courage into a supply that can be gathered and handed over; the word changes from a thing felt in the chest to an act performed before a door.
senses.whyCN: 把名词变成动词，勇气就成了一种可以聚拢、可以递送的东西；这个词从胸腔里感到的状态，变成门前做出的动作。

intro.en: Nerve began as a Latin word for a sinew, and English stretched that cord from anatomy to courage and then to cheek, finally turning it into a verb.
intro.cn: nerve 起初是拉丁语中表示「筋」的词，英语把这条索从解剖拉到勇气、再到厚脸皮，最后还把它变成动词。

items.en: Nervus meant a sinew, tendon or cord, and Roman writers already used it for the cords running inside the body.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、肌腱或细索，古罗马作者已用它指体内穿行的索状结构。

items.en: The adjective nervosus described something sinewy, strong and vigorous, and it is the ancestor of the English word for being tense.
items.cn: 形容词 nervosus 描述充满筋腱、强壮有力的事物，是英语中表示「紧张」那个词的祖先。

items.en: Old French nerf named a nerve or sinew and passed the word to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语 nerf 指神经或筋，在中世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Middle English nerve kept the anatomical sense, while the idea of bodily strength slowly became the idea of mental courage.
items.cn: 中古英语 nerve 保留了解剖义，而「身体有力」的观念慢慢变成了「精神有胆量」。

items.en: Modern English adds the plural sense of tension, the verb of gathering courage, and the judgemental sense of bold impudence.
items.cn: 现代英语添上复数的「紧张不安」义、聚拢勇气的动词义，以及带评判意味的「放肆」义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjectives, adverbs and verbs built on the Latin cord; the near-meaning group holds words for steadiness, boldness and the body's tough tissue.
note.cn: 形近组收建在拉丁语「索」上的形容词、副词与动词；近义组收表示镇定、大胆以及身体坚韧组织的词。

entries.definition: Anxious or easily worried; also relating to the nerves.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑、易担忧的；也与神经有关。

entries.definition: In an anxious or fidgety manner, formed with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以焦虑或坐立不安的方式；由 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being anxious, formed with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑、紧张的状态；由 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: To weaken or drain energy, from Latin e- plus nervus.
entries.definitionCN: 使虚弱、失去活力；来自拉丁语 e- 加 nervus。

entries.definition: The ability to face danger or pain without being stopped by fear.
entries.definitionCN: 面对危险或痛苦而不被恐惧挡住的能力。

entries.definition: Bold determination in a difficult situation, used in lively speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中的大胆决心，多用于口语。

entries.definition: Bold and rude confidence that shocks other people.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆无礼、令旁人吃惊的自信。

entries.definition: A tendon or tough cord of tissue, the original bodily image of nerve.
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱或坚韧的索状组织，是 nerve 最初的身体意象。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin cord of sinew that English turned into a metaphor for courage, and its family keeps both the fibre and the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中一根筋索，英语把它变成勇气的比喻，同族词同时保留纤维与感觉两面。

normal.en: Latin nervus meant sinew or tendon, and the anatomists simply extended that visible cord to the fibres that carry feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nervus 指筋或肌腱，解剖学家只是把这条看得见的索扩展到传递感觉的纤维。

normal.en: Nervous adds -ous to nerve, so it first meant full of sinew and therefore strong, not anxious.
normal.cn: nervous 是 nerve 加 -ous，最初意为「充满筋腱」因而强壮，而不是焦虑。

normal.en: To have the nerve connects courage to the tautness of sinew: a steady body is the picture behind a steady will.
normal.cn: to have the nerve 把勇气与筋的绷紧连起来：稳定的身体正是稳定意志的画面。

normal.en: The plural nerves names the fibres and also the feeling of tension, which is why a case of nerves sounds both medical and emotional.
normal.cn: 复数 nerves 既指纤维，也指紧张的感觉，所以 a case of nerves 听起来既像医学说法又像情绪描述。

normal.en: Nerve as a verb is the noun put to work: to nerve oneself is to gather the taut strength and hold it before acting.
normal.cn: nerve 作动词是名词被派去干活：to nerve oneself 就是聚起那股绷紧的力量，在行动前稳住它。

abstract.en: A word for a physical cord becomes a word for moral steadiness, because courage feels like something pulled tight in the chest.
abstract.cn: 一个指身体细索的词变成了指精神稳定的词，因为勇气感觉像胸腔里有什么被拉紧了。

abstract.en: The distance from courage to cheek is short: both are strength that refuses to be held back by other people's expectations.
abstract.cn: 从勇气到厚脸皮只隔一小步：两者都是不肯被旁人期待挡回去的力量。

abstract.en: Nerve can be a fibre, a feeling, a virtue, an insult and an action, which shows how far one bodily image can travel.
abstract.cn: nerve 可以是纤维、感觉、美德、骂人的话，也可以是一个动作，可见一个身体意象能走多远。

examples.en: A damaged nerve can take months to heal.
examples.cn: 受损的神经可能需要几个月才能愈合。

examples.en: She lost her nerve and stepped back from the edge.
examples.cn: 她失去了勇气，从边缘退了回来。

examples.en: He nerved himself to open the letter.
examples.cn: 他鼓起勇气拆开了那封信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢夫」——神经绷得像一根细线，人也跟着紧张起来；nerve 就是神经、勇气。

root: 拉丁语 nervus（筋、肌腱、神经）经古法语 nerf 进入英语；一般认为与希腊语 neuron（筋、神经）同源，同族词有 nervous、nervously、enervate 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a taut cord in the body; anatomy supplies the fibre, and the tautness supplies courage, cheek, tension and the act of steeling oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体里一根绷紧的索；解剖提供纤维义，绷紧感则提供勇气、厚脸皮、紧张不安与鼓劲这几个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white cord running from the spine to a fingertip, carrying a small electric pulse when touched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细白索从脊柱伸到指尖，被触碰时传过一小阵电流。

branches.en: a nerve cell seen under a microscope
branches.cn: 显微镜下的一枚神经细胞

branches.en: a dentist numbing one side of the jaw
branches.cn: 牙医让半边下颌失去知觉

branches.en: a climber hesitating near the summit
branches.cn: 接近山顶时犹豫的登山者

branches.en: a second request that shocks the room
branches.cn: 让满屋人吃惊的第二次请求

branches.en: a waiting room full of shallow breathing
branches.cn: 满是浅促呼吸的候诊室

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun for sinew, its adjective of strength, the French form that carried it, and the English words that grew from the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「筋」的名词、表示强壮的形容词、承载它的法语形式，以及同一词干上的英语词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the noun for sinew and the adjective for strength, and French passed the noun to English before the metaphor of courage developed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「筋」的名词与「强壮」的形容词，法语把名词传给英语，之后才发展出勇气的比喻。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 巢；窝；（鸟、昆虫等的）巢穴；一窝（雏鸟、卵）；筑巢；嵌套；窝藏
definition_en: a structure built or hollowed out by an animal for laying eggs and raising young
core_image: 树杈间一只用泥与草茎抹成的碗，内壁被压得光滑，四枚带斑点的卵并排躺在正中
scene: 孩子在谷仓梁上发现了一个旧巢，里面还留着去年的一片蛋壳。 A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam, three eggs warm inside it.
sceneCN: 这里 nest 指「鸟巢、窝」（第 1 个义项：动物为产卵育雏而筑的结构）；句意为一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边，里面三枚卵还是温的；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 巢；窝；巢穴；一窝（卵或雏）
筑巢；巢居；嵌套；层层套放

derivatives.zh: 筑巢；筑巢期的
筑巢的鸟；营巢者
巢中雏鸟
嵌套的
巢箱

senses.title: A structure built to hold eggs
senses.titleCN: 为盛放卵而筑成的结构
senses.definition: a structure of twigs, mud, grass or other material in which a bird lays and incubates eggs
senses.definitionCN: 用树枝、泥、草等材料筑成、鸟在其中产卵与孵卵的结构
senses.example: A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边。
senses.why: the core sense is simply the object, because everything else the word names is derived from this built container.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是这件物体，因为这个词命名的其它一切都是由这个容器引申出来的。

senses.title: The home of a whole brood
senses.definition: the place where a brood is reared, viewed as the young family's home
senses.definitionCN: 一窝雏被养育之处，被看作这个幼小家庭的家
senses.example: The whole nest begged whenever the adult landed.
senses.exampleCN: 成鸟一落下，整窝雏鸟都乞食。
senses.why: the container and its occupants merge, so nest may name the family inside as much as the structure.
senses.whyCN: 容器与其居住者合并，因此 nest 既可指结构，也可指里面的全家。

senses.title: A clutch counted as one unit
senses.definition: the set of eggs laid in one nest and incubated together
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中产出并一起孵化的一组卵
senses.example: Rangers recorded a nest of four eggs under the lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 巡护员在灯下记录到一窝四枚卵。
senses.why: counting by nests is convenient because the nest defines the set, so the container becomes the unit of number.
senses.whyCN: 以巢计数很方便，因为巢定义了这一组，容器于是成了计数单位。

senses.title: A hollow made by another animal
senses.titleCN: 由其它动物挖出的巢穴
senses.definition: a burrow, hole or cavity used by an insect, mammal or fish for young
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫、哺乳动物或鱼为育幼而使用的洞、穴或腔
senses.example: Wasps build a paper nest under the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂在屋瓦下筑成纸质的巢。
senses.why: once the word is applied beyond birds, the structure stops being woven and becomes any prepared cavity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦越出鸟类，这个结构就不再是编织的，而成为任何备好的腔室。

senses.title: To build and occupy a nest
senses.definition: to build a nest and use it for breeding
senses.definitionCN: 建造巢并将其用于繁殖
senses.example: Swallows nest every year in the same corner of the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 燕子每年都在谷仓同一个角落筑巢。
senses.why: the verb is simply the noun turned into an action, so it means to do what the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转为动作，意为做出名词所指的那件事。

senses.title: To place one thing inside another
senses.titleCN: 把一物套进另一物内部
senses.definition: to fit objects or structures one inside another, as boxes or data tables
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或结构放进彼此内部，如盒子或数据表
senses.example: Nest the smaller boxes inside the larger crate.
senses.exampleCN: 把小盒子套进大板条箱里。
senses.why: the technical sense generalizes the shape of the bird's cup: something held within something else.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把鸟巢的形状一般化：一物被另一物容纳在其中。

senses.title: A graduated set that fits inside itself
senses.titleCN: 可以逐层套放的一组器物
senses.definition: a set of similar objects of decreasing size that store one inside another, as a nest of tables
senses.definitionCN: 一组大小递减、可以互相套放的同类物件，如套几
senses.example: The nest of tables slotted under the largest one.
senses.exampleCN: 套几收进最大的那张下面。
senses.why: the noun is applied to objects that imitate the containment of a nest, so the name follows the shape rather than the bird.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词被用于模仿「巢的容纳关系」的物件，因此名称追随形状而非鸟。

senses.title: A den of troublesome people or things
senses.titleCN: 滋生麻烦的人或事物之处
senses.definition: a place or group seen as a breeding ground for something harmful, as in a nest of thieves
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有害之物滋生地的场所或群体，如贼窝
senses.example: The yard had become a nest of infection after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后这个院子成了感染滋生地。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the idea of a sheltered place where something grows, and that something is no longer young.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留「有遮蔽之处、某种东西在其中生长」的意思，而生长之物已不再是幼鸟。

intro.en: Nest is an Old English word, nest, with the same form in several old Germanic languages; its relation to Latin nidus is debated rather than settled.
intro.cn: nest 是古英语词 nest，在数种古老日耳曼语中形式相同；它与拉丁 nidus 的关系属争议，未有定论。

items.en: Old English nest named both the structure and the brood in it, and the word has kept that double reach.
items.cn: 古英语 nest 既指结构，也指其中的一窝，这双重范围一直保留。

items.en: Old Norse nest, Old High German nest and Middle Dutch nest show a common Germanic stock, so Latin borrowing is unlikely.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 nest、古高地德语 nest、中古荷兰语 nest 表明共同的日耳曼来源，因此不太可能是拉丁借词。

items.en: Latin nidus 'nest' looks similar and means the same, but most handbooks treat the resemblance as parallel; a shared Indo-European source is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，但多数辞书把这种相似视为平行；共有印欧来源属重构形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Germanic shape of nest is unresolved; the root commonly printed for it is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：nest 在日耳曼语之前的形式无定论；常印出的词根是重构形式，并非有证材料。

items.en: The verb nest appeared later, formed directly from the noun, and was extended to any placing of one thing inside another.
items.cn: 动词 nest 出现较晚，直接由名词构成，并被扩展到任何把一物放进另一物的动作。

items.en: Phrases such as empty nest and nest egg carried the word into family life and household finance.
items.cn: empty nest、nest egg 等短语把这个词带进家庭生活与家庭理财。

note.en: Group one separates the near-synonyms for animal homes; group two separates the words built on nest itself.
note.cn: 第一组区分表示动物居所近义词；第二组区分由 nest 本身构成的词。

entries.definition: The -ing form names the building and sitting; the bare nest names the object.
entries.definitionCN: -ing 形式指建与伏的行为；原形 nest 指物件。

entries.definition: A nestling is a chick too young to leave; it is the content of the nest, not the nest.
entries.definitionCN: nestling 是尚不能离巢的雏鸟，是巢中之物，而非巢。

entries.definition: A nester is the bird regarded as the one that nests, marked by -er.
entries.definitionCN: nester 是把鸟看作筑巢者，由 -er 标记。

entries.definition: Nested describes something already placed inside another; it is a state, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: nested 描述已被放进另一物之中的状态，是状态而非地点。

entries.definition: A burrow is dug into earth or sand; a nest may be built on a branch or in a hole.
entries.definitionCN: burrow 掘入土或沙；巢可能筑在枝上或洞里。

entries.definition: A den is a mammal's shelter, often a cave or hollow, and usually not built from gathered material.
entries.definitionCN: den 是哺乳动物的居所，常为洞穴，通常不由采集材料筑成。

entries.definition: A lair is where a wild animal rests, especially a predator; it carries no idea of eggs.
entries.definitionCN: lair 是野兽尤其捕食者歇息之处，不含产卵之意。

entries.definition: A hive is the home of a bee colony, a special case of an insect nest with a fixed architecture.
entries.definitionCN: hive 是蜂群的家，是昆虫巢的一种特例，结构固定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Germanic relatives, real compounds and real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的日耳曼同族词、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: The Germanic relatives are Old Norse nest and Old High German nest, not Latin words.
normal.cn: 日耳曼同族词是古诺斯语 nest 与古高地德语 nest，而非拉丁词。

normal.en: The family runs nest, nesting, nester, nestling, nested, nest box.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nest、nesting、nester、nestling、nested、nest box。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: build a nest, leave the nest, nest of eggs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：筑巢、离巢、一窝蛋。

normal.en: The idioms empty nest and nest egg show the word applied to family and savings.
normal.cn: 习语 empty nest 与 nest egg 显示这个词被用于家庭与储蓄。

normal.en: In computing, nest means to place one structure inside another.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，nest 指把一种结构放进另一种。

abstract.en: Picture a cup so exactly shaped that the sitter's body closes its opening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗形制精准，伏者的身体正好封住开口。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose walls keep growing back after each departure.
abstract.cn: 想象一座屋子，每次有人离开后墙壁又重新长回。

abstract.en: Picture a set of bowls where the smallest is invisible until lifted out.
abstract.cn: 想象一套碗，最小的一只不被提起就看不见。

examples.en: The nest was rebuilt on the same branch after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，巢又在同一根枝上重建。

examples.en: She found an old nest in the rafters, empty and crumbling.
examples.cn: 她在椽子上发现一只空了的旧巢，正在崩解。

examples.en: Programmers nest these records inside a parent object.
examples.cn: 程序员把这些记录嵌进一个父对象里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nest（巢）」——树枝围成碗，卵卧其中 → 巢、窝；动作义为筑巢、套住

root: 古英语 nest「巢；一窝」，与古诺斯语、古高地德语、中古荷兰语 nest 同出日耳曼共有词；与拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，通常视为平行构词，共有印欧来源仅为重构形式，日耳曼以前词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a built cup holds something precious, and the word then names the occupants, the count, a prepared cavity, a den of trouble, the act of building, any placing of one thing inside another, and finally a set of objects made to slot together.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形状展开：一只编成的碗托住贵重之物，词语随后指其居住者、计数单位、备好的腔室、滋生麻烦的窝、建造动作、任何把一物放进另一物的动作，最后指一组可以互相套放的器物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup woven at the branch fork, its inner walls smoothed by the body inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝杈分叉处编成的碗，内壁被其中的身体压得光滑。

branches.en: CUP AND FAMILY: the container and the family in it are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 碗与家庭：容器与其中的家庭由同一个词命名。

branches.en: COUNTED SET: the nest defines the clutch, so the container becomes the unit.
branches.cn: 可数的组：巢定义了这一窝，容器于是成了单位。

branches.en: A SHELTERED PLACE: any animal's cavity, and a den where trouble breeds.
branches.cn: 有遮蔽之处：任何动物的腔室，以及滋生麻烦的窝。

branches.en: DOING THE NOUN: the verb is the noun turned into an act.
branches.cn: 做名词所指的事：动词就是名词转为动作。

branches.en: SHAPE EXPORTED: a rule for holding one thing inside another, and objects made to nest.
branches.cn: 形状外输：一条「一物容另一物」的规则，以及照此造出的套叠器物。

intro.en: Nest is a bare Germanic root that takes English suffixes and compounds; it has no Latin prefix structure.
intro.cn: nest 是裸露的日耳曼词根，只接英语后缀与复合成分，没有拉丁前缀结构。

latinIntro.en: Nest itself has no Latin element; the Latin entries are the learned equivalents English borrowed separately for the same content.
latinIntro.cn: nest 本身不含拉丁成分；下列拉丁条目是英语为同一内容另行借入的学术词。

items.example: They used the bonus as a nest egg.
items.exampleCN: 他们把奖金当作储备金。

items.meaning: a home after the children leave
items.example: The empty nest felt too quiet.

items.exampleCN: 志愿者挂上了四十只巢箱。

items.example: The ruling stirred a hornet's nest.

definition_zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉；广播网；联网
definition_en: an interconnected system of lines, people, or devices, or to connect things into such a system
core_image: 一张撒开的渔网：每个网结都连着别的网结
scene: 渔网摊在甲板上，一个个网结彼此相连，把每个部分都串成一片。A fishing net lies spread across the deck, and its knots form a network that links every part to the next.
sceneCN: 这里 network 是「网状结构、网络」（第 1 个义项：由线或节点交织成的网）；句意：一张渔网摊在甲板上，网结连成一张网，把每一处都连到下一处。图中可辨识物件：渔网、网结、甲板、缆绳、渔船；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉网；广播网
用网覆盖；联网；建立人脉

derivatives.zh: 联网；建立人脉；网络化（network 的动名词）
联网的；网状的
善于建立人脉的人
网；网材（net 加 -ing）
网；罗网；用网捕（network 的第一成分）
互联网（inter- 加 net）

senses.title: A mesh of connected lines: netting
senses.titleCN: 连成一片的网线：网状织物
senses.definition: a structure of cords or threads crossed and knotted so that every part is linked to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 由绳线交叉打结而成的结构，每一处都与其他部分相连
senses.example: A torn network of netting lay across the harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 一张破了的网摊在港口的石头上。
senses.why: Network began in the 1550s as net plus work, literally a net-like fabric or structure. The picture is physical: knots joined by threads.
senses.whyCN: network 在 16 世纪 50 年代由 net 加 work 构成，字面是“网一样的织物或结构”。画面是实体的：网结被网线连起来。

senses.title: An interlocking transport system
senses.definition: a system of rivers, canals, roads, or railways that cross and connect at many points
senses.definitionCN: 河流、运河、道路或铁路在许多点上交叉相连的系统
senses.example: A network of canals linked the inland farms to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 一张运河网把内陆农场与港口连了起来。
senses.why: The 1839 sense 'any complex, interlocking system' was first used of rivers, canals and railways. The mesh becomes a map of routes.
senses.whyCN: 1839 年出现的“任何复杂交织的系统”一义，最初用于河流、运河与铁路。实体的网变成了一张路线图。

senses.title: A broadcasting system of many transmitters
senses.titleCN: 由多个发射台组成的广播网
senses.definition: a group of radio or television stations that share programmes and transmit them over a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 共享节目、向广大地区播送的广播电台或电视台群体
senses.example: The radio network broadcast the speech to forty stations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家广播网把演讲播送到四十家电台。
senses.why: From 1914 the word named a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters. Signals travel from node to node, so the mesh becomes a web of stations.
senses.whyCN: 从 1914 年起，这个词指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。信号从一个节点传到另一个节点，网于是变成了一张电台之网。

senses.title: An interconnected group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who are connected through work, family, or shared interests and can help one another
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、家庭或共同兴趣相连、能互相帮助的一群人
senses.example: Her network of former classmates helped her find work.
senses.exampleCN: 她由老同学组成的人脉网帮她找到了工作。
senses.why: The 1934 sense came from psychology: people as nodes, relationships as threads. The mesh is now social rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 1934 年的义项来自心理学术语：人是节点，关系是网线。此时网是社会性的，而非实体的。

senses.title: A computer network: machines that talk
senses.titleCN: 计算机网络：会互相通信的机器
senses.definition: a set of computers and devices connected so that they can exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 为交换数据而连接起来的一组计算机与设备
senses.example: The lab's computers share one network and one printer.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室的计算机共用一个网络和一台打印机。
senses.why: When computers became nodes, the old mesh needed no new shape: each machine is a knot, each cable a thread. The word kept its picture and changed its material.
senses.whyCN: 当计算机成为节点时，这张网不需要新形状：每台机器是一个结，每根线缆是一根网线。词保留了画面，只换了材料。

senses.title: A utility grid: power and telephone lines
senses.titleCN: 公用事业网：电力与电话线路
senses.definition: the connected system of cables, pipes, or lines that carries power, water, or telephone signals
senses.definitionCN: 输送电力、水或电话信号的互联电缆、管道或线路系统
senses.example: The power network failed during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间电网瘫痪了。
senses.why: A grid is a mesh laid over a region. Power lines join substations as knots join threads, so network names any utility system with that shape.
senses.whyCN: 电网是铺在一片区域上的网。电线把变电站连起来，正如网线把网结连起来，因此 network 可指任何具此形状的公用系统。

senses.title: To cover with a net
senses.definition: to cover an area or object with netting, usually for protection
senses.definitionCN: 用网覆盖一片区域或一个物体，通常是为了保护
senses.example: They networked the orchard to keep the birds off the fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用网罩住果园，防止鸟啄食果实。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1887 with the plainest sense: to put a net over something. It turns the noun's object into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义于 1887 年出现，意思最直白：把网盖在某物上。它把名词所指的对象变成了一个动作。

senses.title: To broadcast across a network
senses.definition: to send a programme out through several linked stations at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时通过多家相连的电台或电视台播送节目
senses.example: The show was networked across the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节目通过广播网在全国播送。
senses.why: From 1940 the verb meant to distribute a programme through a network of transmitters. The broadcast travels along every thread of the mesh.
senses.whyCN: 从 1940 年起，动词指通过发射台网络分发节目。广播沿着这张网的每一根线传出去。

senses.title: To connect computers together
senses.definition: to link computers or devices so that they can share data
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机或设备连接起来，使它们能共享数据
senses.example: Engineers networked the two sites with fibre-optic cable.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用光纤把两个站点联网。
senses.why: The 1972 computing sense turns the noun into a task: you tie new knots into the existing mesh until the machines can reach one another.
senses.whyCN: 1972 年的计算机义把名词变成一个任务：你把新的结系进已有的网里，直到机器能彼此抵达。

senses.title: To build professional contacts
senses.definition: to meet and cultivate useful contacts, especially for work
senses.definitionCN: 结识并经营有用的人脉，尤指为工作目的
senses.example: She networks at every conference she attends.
senses.exampleCN: 她每参加一次会议就经营一次人脉。
senses.why: The 1982 sense applies the verb to people: each new acquaintance is a knot added to a personal mesh. Nothing physical remains but the shape.
senses.whyCN: 1982 年的义项把动词用在人身上：每位新认识的人都是加入个人之网的一个结。实体消失了，只剩形状。

intro.en: Network is a plain English compound of net and work, first recorded in the 1550s for net-like fabric. Its modern senses are a series of metaphors laid on that mesh: transport in 1839, broadcasting in 1914, people in 1934, and finally computers.
intro.cn: network 是 net 与 work 的朴素英语复合词，16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，指网一样的织物。它的现代义项是一层层叠加在这张网上的比喻：1839 年的交通、1914 年的广播、1934 年的人群，最后是计算机。

items.en: Net is Old English net 'net, snare', a word old enough to serve as a metaphor for a moral or mental trap.
items.cn: net 是古英语 net“网、罗网”，这个词古老到可以被用作道德或心理陷阱的比喻。

items.en: Network is first recorded in the 1550s as net plus work, meaning a net-like fabric or structure.
items.cn: network 于 16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，由 net 加 work 构成，指网一样的织物或结构。

items.en: The sense 'any complex, interlocking system' appears in 1839, first applied to networks of rivers, canals and railways.
items.cn: “任何复杂交织的系统”一义出现于 1839 年，最初用于河流、运河与铁路的网络。

items.en: A network becomes a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters in 1914.
items.cn: 1914 年，network 开始指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。

items.en: The sense 'interconnected group of people' appears in 1934 as psychological jargon.
items.cn: “彼此相连的人群”一义于 1934 年出现，原为心理学术语。

items.en: The verb follows: to cover with a net in 1887, to broadcast in 1940, to link computers in 1972, and to build contacts in 1982.
items.cn: 动词随后跟进：1887 年“用网覆盖”，1940 年“通过广播网播送”，1972 年“计算机联网”，1982 年“建立人脉”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, including a phrase that sounds like network; the second group is chosen for the mesh image they share.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与读音挑选，其中有一个听起来像 network 的短语；第二组按它们共享的网状意象挑选。

entries.definition: the total value of assets minus liabilities. The phrase sounds almost like network but belongs to finance, not to nets.
entries.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债。这个短语听起来几乎和 network 一样，但属于财务，与网无关。

entries.definition: a small, low-cost laptop of the late 2000s. It joins net to book, not to work.
entries.definitionCN: 21 世纪末流行的小型低价笔记本电脑。它把 net 与 book 组合，而不是与 work 组合。

entries.definition: material made of net or mesh. It is the noun from net, not a form of network.
entries.definitionCN: 网材；网。它是 net 派生的名词，不是 network 的变形。

entries.definition: a mesh spun by a spider, or any complex system of linked parts. It stresses threads woven by a maker, while network stresses nodes joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 蜘蛛结的网，或任何由相连部分构成的复杂系统。它强调由造物者织出的线，而 network 强调节点之间的连接。

entries.definition: a pattern of crossing lines, especially for power or streets. It is regular and geometric, while a network can grow irregularly.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉线构成的格网，尤指电网或街道网。它是规则、几何的，而 network 可以不规则地生长。

entries.definition: a material of connected strands with open spaces between them. It names the fabric itself rather than the system it forms.
entries.definitionCN: 由相连线股构成、中间有空隙的材料。它指织物本身，而不是织物形成的系统。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: net plus work in 1550s, then the dated extensions to transport, broadcasting, people and computers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：16 世纪 50 年代的 net 加 work，随后是有年代可查的扩展——交通、广播、人群与计算机。

normal.en: net plus work says the whole thing plainly: work made of net, a net-like fabric.
normal.cn: net 加 work 说得很直白：用网做成的制成品，即网一样的织物。

normal.en: In 1839 the mesh became a map: rivers, canals and railways crossing at many points.
normal.cn: 1839 年，这张网变成了一张地图：河流、运河与铁路在许多点上交叉。

normal.en: In 1914 the mesh became stations: many transmitters sharing one broadcast.
normal.cn: 1914 年，这张网变成了电台：多个发射台共享一次广播。

normal.en: In 1934 people became the nodes, and in 1972 computers did: the shape stayed, the material changed.
normal.cn: 1934 年人成了节点，1972 年计算机成了节点：形状没变，材料变了。

normal.en: The verbs follow the nouns: cover with a net, broadcast, connect, and build contacts.
normal.cn: 动词跟随名词：用网覆盖、播送、联网、建立人脉。

abstract.en: Picture one knot with four threads leaving it: remove the threads and it is only a knot; the connections are what make it a network.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网结向四面伸出四根线：抽掉线，它只是个结；正是连接使它成为网络。

abstract.en: The same drawing works for a map, a radio system, a group of friends, and a room of servers.
abstract.cn: 同一幅图可以画成地图、广播系统、朋友圈，也可以画成一屋子的服务器。

abstract.en: Cut one thread and the mesh still holds: a network is judged by how many routes remain, not by any single knot.
abstract.cn: 剪断一根线，网仍然撑得住：网络的价值在于还剩多少条通路，而不在任何一个结。

examples.en: A dense network of trails connects the villages along the valley.
examples.cn: 一张密集的小路网连接着山谷里的村庄。

examples.en: The company rebuilt its computer network after the outage.
examples.cn: 停电事故后，公司重建了计算机网络。

examples.en: He spent the conference networking with editors and researchers.
examples.cn: 他在会议上忙着与编辑和研究人员建立人脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内特网」——内里特别多网结，四面八方都连着 → network 网络、人脉

root: 由古英语 net“网、罗网”加 work“工作、制成品”复合而成，1550s 首次记录，核心是“网一样的连结结构”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of network all keep one shape: knots joined by threads. The material changes from cord to canals, transmitters, people, cables and computers, and the verb senses simply put the mesh into action.
sensesIntro.cn: network 的十个义项都保留同一个形状：网结被网线连起来。材料从绳索换成运河、发射台、人、电缆与计算机，动词义只是让这张网动起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fishing net spread out, every knot tied to others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张摊开的渔网，每个网结都连着别的结。

branches.en: FROM FABRIC TO MAP: literal netting, then a system of rivers, canals and railways.
branches.cn: 从织物到地图：字面的网，然后是河流、运河与铁路构成的系统。

branches.en: FROM STATIONS TO PEOPLE: transmitters sharing programmes, then people sharing contacts.
branches.cn: 从电台到人：共享节目的发射台，然后是共享关系的人。

branches.en: TECHNICAL GRIDS: computers exchanging data, and utility lines carrying power or signals.
branches.cn: 技术性网络：交换数据的计算机，以及输送电力或信号的公用线路。

branches.en: THE OLD VERBS: covering with netting, and sending a programme through many stations.
branches.cn: 较早的动词：用网覆盖，以及通过多家电台播送节目。

branches.en: THE MODERN VERBS: linking machines, and cultivating a personal web of contacts.
branches.cn: 现代动词：连接机器，以及经营个人的关系网。

intro.en: Network is the compound net plus work, with no Latin suffix. English adds -ing, -ed, -er and -able to it, and the same net appears in internet, intranet, netting and netbook.
intro.cn: network 是 net 加 work 的复合词，不含拉丁后缀。英语在它上面加 -ing、-ed、-er、-able，而同一个 net 也出现在 internet、intranet、netting、netbook 中。

latinIntro.en: Network is Germanic, not Latin. The Latin entries below are its nearest counterparts, given for contrast: rete 'net', nexus 'a binding', and nectere 'to bind'.
latinIntro.cn: network 属日耳曼语，不属拉丁语。下面列出的拉丁词是它最接近的对应词，仅供对照：rete“网”、nexus“联结”、nectere“捆缚”。

items.meaning: a mesh-like structure or connected system
items.meaningCN: 网状结构；相连的系统（net“网”+ work“制成品”）
items.example: The city's tram network covers the whole centre.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市的有轨电车网络覆盖了整个市中心。

items.meaning: the act of linking systems or building contacts
items.meaningCN: 联网；建立人脉（-ing 构成动名词）
items.example: Networking is half of the value of a conference.
items.exampleCN: 建立人脉是一场会议一半的价值。

items.meaningCN: 联网的；连成网的（-ed 构成形容词）

items.meaning: a person skilled at building contacts
items.meaningCN: 善于建立人脉的人（-er 构成人称名词）
items.example: She is the best networker in the sales team.
items.exampleCN: 她是销售团队里最会经营人脉的人。

items.meaning: a mesh of cord used to catch things
items.meaningCN: 网；罗网（network 的第一成分）
items.example: The fishermen repaired the net before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔民在黎明前修补了渔网。

items.meaningCN: 网材；网（-ing 构成材料名词）
items.example: Netting protected the young trees from deer.
items.exampleCN: 网罩保护了小树不被鹿啃食。

items.meaningCN: 互联网（inter-“在……之间”+ net“网络”）
items.example: The files were sent over the internet.

items.meaning: a private network inside an organisation
items.meaningCN: 内联网（intra-“在内部”+ net“网络”）
items.example: Staff read the policy on the company intranet.
items.exampleCN: 员工在公司内联网上读到这项政策。

items.meaning: a small laptop designed mainly for online use
items.meaningCN: 上网本（net“网络”+ book，指主要用于上网的小电脑）
items.example: He carried a netbook instead of a full laptop.
items.exampleCN: 他带了一台上网本，而不是完整的笔记本电脑。

items.meaning: capable of being connected to a network
items.meaningCN: 可联网的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The printer is networkable and shared by the office.
items.exampleCN: 这台打印机可联网，供全办公室共用。

latinEntries.meaning: a net, a network of cords

latinEntries.meaningCN: 联结；联系（来自 nectere“捆缚”）
